'''''Bougainvillea spectabilis''''', also known as '''great bougainvillea''',<ref name=plants/> is a species of flowering plant. It is native to [[Brazil]], [[Bolivia]], [[Peru]], and [[Argentina]]'s [[Chubut Province]].<ref name=arsgrin>{{GRIN | accessdate=20 December 2014}}</ref><ref name="Lim2014">{{cite book|author=T. K. Lim|title=Edible Medicinal and Non Medicinal Plants, Volume 8: Flowers|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=-nvGBAAAQBAJ&pg=PA495|date=1 January 2014|publisher=Springer Science & Business|isbn=978-94-017-8748-2|pages=489–494}}</ref> It  is  widely grown as an ornamental plant.<ref name="Lim2014"/>
==Description==
''Bougainvillea spectabilis'' grows as a woody vine or shrub, reaching {{convert|15|to|40|ft|m}}<ref name=tropicosbolivia>{{cite web|title=Tropicos|url=http://www.tropicos.org/Name/22500248?projectid=13|website=tropicos.org|accessdate=20 December 2014}}</ref><ref name="Jarrett2003"/> with heart-shaped leaves and thorny, pubescent stems.<ref name="Jarrett2003"/> The flowers are generally small, white, and inconspicuous, highlighted by several brightly colored modified leaves called [[bract]]s. The bracts can vary in color, ranging from white, red, mauve, purple-red, or orange. Its fruit is a small, inconspicuous, dry, elongated achene.<ref name="Lim2014"/><ref name="Jarrett2003"/>

==Distribution==
[[File:Bougainvillée Generalife Espagne.jpg|thumb|right|''Bougainvillea spectabilis'']]
[[File:Starr 030418-0059 Bougainvillea spectabilis.jpg|thumb|Detail of flowers and bracts]]
[[File:Plaza Gral Ángel Pacheco - Ciudad de General Pacheco (Partido de Tigre)-2.JPG|thumb|right|In the [[province of Buenos Aires]]]]

''Bougainvillea spectabilis'' is native to Brazil, Peru, Bolivia, and [[Chubut Province]], Argentina, but it has been introduced in many other areas.<ref name="Lim2014"/>

==Cultivation==
''Bougainvillea spectabilis'' can grow in [[hardiness zone]]s 10–11, preferring full sun, dry conditions, and fertile soil.<ref name="Jarrett2003">{{cite book|author=Amanda Jarrett|title=Ornamental Tropical Shrubs|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=-t-OAWurUdcC&pg=PA27|year=2003|publisher=Pineapple Press Inc|isbn=978-1-56164-275-5|page=27}}</ref> It can be propagated from stem and root cuttings.<ref name="Lim2014"/>

==Traditional medicine==
The Yanadi tribe of [[Chittoor district]], [[Andhra Pradesh]], India, once used the leaves of ''Bougainvillea spectabilis'' to heal [[diabetes]].{{cn|date=April 2024}}
